mechanism: Leflunomide may impair vitamin D metabolism and increase risk of bone loss; vitamin D deficiency is common in rheumatoid arthritis patients on leflunomide due to malabsorption and immunosuppression effects.
action: Monitor vitamin D levels periodically in patients on leflunomide; maintain adequate vitamin D supplementation (typically 800-2000 IU daily) and ensure sufficient calcium intake to prevent bone loss and osteoporosis.
